angle: Sweep the clustering resolution r from 2 to n and compare the exact minimum cross-edge count against the toll k(r-1): three K5 islands joined by three single bridges pass the cut test (r=2) AND the headcount test (r=n) yet fail at r=3, proving that the Nash-Williams-Tutte condition genuinely quantifies over every partition because sparsity can hide at an intermediate resolution — then 2k-edge-connectivity is shown to be the cheap sufficient condition via double counting.

libraries.name: cytoscape
libraries.role: renders every clustered graph view: a partition is drawn as cytoscape COMPOUND PARENT NODES (one labelled box per part) with the vertices at hand-authored preset positions, re-clustering is node.move({parent}) plus empty-parent removal, cross vs internal edges are edge classes recoloured on every change, click-to-recluster is a tap handler on node.v, and the contracted quotient multigraph G/P is a second instance using curve-style:bezier so parallel cross edges fan out

libraries.name: echarts
libraries.role: the centrepiece resolution-scan chart (two stacked grids sharing one category axis r: bars of exact minimum cross edges + dashed toll line k(r-1) on top, diverging slack bars below, linked axisPointer, per-item status colours, a markPoint annotating only the FIRST failing r, and a click handler that loads that r's minimising partition into the graph); also the live toll meters (horizontal 2-bar comparison of cross edges vs toll) and the 1-bridge-vs-2-bridges comparison line chart

libraries.name: katex
libraries.role: renders the iff-statement of the theorem, the contraction/toll implication chain T -> T/P -> >= r-1, the r=2 specialisation to k-edge-connectivity, the r=n headcount, the 2k-edge-connectivity corollary, the double-counting line e_G(P) = 1/2 sum |delta(V_i)| >= kr > k(r-1), and the closing min-over-partitions restatement

building_blocks: graph descriptor {id, name, n, edges:[[u,v]], pos:[[x,y]], labels, groups?, bridgeIdx?} with hand-authored preset layouts
buildCycle(n, R): cycle graph on a regular n-gon

buildIslands(b): three K5 islands at the corners of a triangle joined pairwise by b bridges, with bridge endpoints chosen geometrically as the unused vertices nearest the target island's centre, returning bridgeIdx so the bridges can be emphasised
buildPetersen(): outer 5-cycle + inner pentagram + spokes on two concentric polar rings
completeEdges(ids), adjacency(g): edge list of a clique on given ids; adjacency lists with multiplicity
crossCount(g, part) and crossEdgeIdx(g, part): cross-edge count and index list for an arbitrary vertex->part map
normalize(part) / partsOf(part) / rOf(part): canonical relabelling of a partition to 0,1,2,... in order of first appearance, sorted part ids, and r
minCutExhaustive(g): enumerate all 2^(n-1)-1 bipartitions, return {min, part, checked}
partDegrees(g, part): per-part {p, size, deg} where deg = |delta(V_i)|, the double-counting tally

heuristicMinR(g, adj, r, restarts, rng): randomised restart + single-vertex-move local search for a low-cross partition into exactly r parts, never emptying a part; returns a genuine partition (used only as a pruning seed)

exactMinR(g, adj, r, seedBest, nodeBudget): EXACT minimum cross-edge count over all partitions into exactly r parts by DFS over restricted-growth strings with branch-and-bound (monotone partial cross count vs incumbent, plus a 'can still reach r parts' cut); returns {min, part, complete, nodes, found} and reports truncation honestly
fullScan(g): complete brute force over every set partition (Bell(n)) returning min cross edges and an argmin per r — the cross-check for small graphs
resolutionScan(g, restarts, seed): heuristic-seeded exact scan for every r in 2..n, aggregating DFS node counts, completeness and elapsed ms
makeDSU(n): path-compressed disjoint-set forest
greedyPack(g, k, tries, rng): randomised first-fit edge-disjoint forest packer returning {col, cnt, score, target}, explicitly labelled a heuristic
makeRNG(seed): xorshift32 so every reload reports identical numbers

makeGraphView(hostId, graph, opts): cytoscape clustered-graph widget — preset positions, compound cluster boxes created/removed on demand, setPartition(part, isShort), setShort(v), paintTrees(col), noBoxes/emphasize options for static specimen views, onVertexTap callback, fit()
makeQuotientView(hostId): cytoscape contracted-multigraph widget, .render(graph, part, short) placing r super-nodes on a circle and fanning the cross edges as bezier parallel edges

CY_STYLE: cytoscape stylesheet with node.v / node.cluster (round-rectangle compound box, top-anchored label) / node.qn (quotient super-node) / edge / edge.cross / edge.cross.short / edge.emph / edge.t0 / edge.t1 / edge.dim
verdict(min, req) -> {key, glyph, word, colour}: the single source of truth for pass / exactly-on-the-toll / short, reused by chips, tooltips, bars and logs so colour is never the only channel
scanOption(rows, k, opt): ECharts option for the two-grid resolution scan (bars + dashed toll line + diverging slack strip, shared axisPointer, first-failure markPoint, optional click-to-load)
meterOption(cross, req, k, r): ECharts horizontal 2-bar toll meter with value labels and a status-coloured actual bar
LEGEND_HTML(extra): plain-HTML swatch legend pairing every status colour with its glyph and words
stat(label, value) / chip(verdict): stat tile and verdict pill (dot + glyph + text)
tex(nodeOrId, texString, displayMode): KaTeX render helper with throwOnError:false
deferred job queue: heavy computations pushed onto a jobs[] array and run one per setTimeout tick after first paint, with .busy placeholders swapped in beforehand
debounced onResize that calls chart.resize() and cy.resize()+cy.fit() on every live instance

fold-down page skeleton: hero + numbered .beat sections, each with .beat-head (number / title / thesis) and an optional .split (wide-left / wide-right) grid collapsing at 900px, plus .panel / .callout / .log / .readout primitives
computations: exhaustive minimum cut on 3xK5 by enumerating all 16383 bipartitions of 15 vertices -> min cut 2, so the graph is exactly 2-edge-connected and meets the r=2 requirement k=2 with zero slack
exhaustive minimum cut on C6 (31 bipartitions -> 2) and on Petersen (511 bipartitions -> 3 = 2k-1 for k=2)
headcount test on 3xK5: m = 33 >= k(n-1) = 2*14 = 28, slack +5

EXACT minimum cross-edge count over all partitions into exactly r parts, for every r from 2 to 15 on 3xK5, by branch-and-bound over restricted-growth strings; every branch resolves (no node-budget truncation) so all 14 values are proved minima, with per-r surviving DFS node counts printed
the certificate: exact minimum at r=3 on 3xK5 is 3 < k(r-1) = 4, and the minimiser returned by the search is exactly the three-island partition whose cross edges are the three bridges
the full k=2 scan on 3xK5 is 2,3,7,10,12,13,17,20,22,23,27,30,32,33 against tolls 2,4,6,...,28 — exactly one negative slack, at r=3
complete brute force over all Bell(6) = 203 partitions of C6: min cross per r = 2,3,4,5,6 for r = 2..6, failing from r=3 onward and also at r=6 (6 < 10)
complete brute force over all Bell(10) = 115975 partitions of the Petersen graph: first resolution short is r = 8 (13 < 14), two resolutions before the r = 10 headcount (15 < 18)
exact resolution scan of the doubled-bridge graph 3xK5 with 2 bridges per pair: min cut rises to 4 = 2k and every r clears the toll with slack >= 2
per-part double-counting tally on the live clustering: |V_i|, delta(V_i), the test delta(V_i) >= 2k, the identity sum delta(V_i) = 2 e_G(P), and the resulting bound e_G(P) >= kr > k(r-1)

randomised first-fit packing, 6000 restarts: 27/28 tree edges on the one-bridge graph (labelled a heuristic, not a proof) and 28/28 on the two-bridge graph, delivering two explicit edge-disjoint spanning trees
live cross-edge count, r, toll k(r-1), slack and verdict recomputed on every user edit of the partition
interactions: click any vertex in the C6 lab or the island lab to move it into the next cluster (a new cluster is created when you pass the last one); the cluster boxes, cross-edge highlighting, quotient multigraph, toll meter, four stat tiles and the verdict chip all recompute
C6 cluster presets: all-one / two-halves / three-arcs / every-vertex-alone

switch k in {1,2,3} in either lab: the toll line, the meter, the stats, the verdict and the scan-chart caption update while the exact-minimum bars stay put (they are properties of the graph, not of k)
click any bar in the resolution scan to load that r's exact minimising clustering into the graph below and scroll to it
hover the resolution scan for a linked crosshair tooltip giving r, the cheapest clustering's cross-edge count, the toll, the slack and the verdict
island presets: jump to the min cut (r=2), the three islands (r=3), every-vertex-alone (r=15), all-one
toggle bridges per pair between 1 and 2 in section 06: the graph is rebuilt, the min cut readout and the per-part delta tally recompute, the clustering resets to r=3 and the packer log clears
section 06 clustering presets: cluster-by-island / min-cut / all-alone, each redrawing the per-part double-count table

run the randomised packer (6000 restarts): the best packing is painted onto the graph as two edge-coloured spanning forests and the log reports edges placed per tree, elapsed ms, and whether the result is a genuine packing
hover the 1-bridge-vs-2-bridges comparison chart for a three-way tooltip (toll, 1 bridge, 2 bridges) with per-series pass/fail glyphs
assets: lib/fonts/KaTeX_*.woff2 (all 20 faces: AMS, Caligraphic, Fraktur, Main, Math, SansSerif, Script, Size1-4, Typewriter)
gotchas: ESM-only packages fail from file:// (origin null triggers CORS), so all three libraries are the plain UMD dist builds loaded by classic <script> tags — verified by opening the page over file:// in headless Chrome with Runtime/Log domains enabled and asserting zero exceptions and zero console errors

Web Workers cannot be used from file:// in Chrome (the worker script load is cross-origin), so the ~200 ms branch-and-bound and the ~120 ms Bell(10) brute force run on the main thread; they are pushed onto a jobs[] queue and drained one job per setTimeout(0) tick after first paint, with .busy placeholders in the chart hosts so nothing looks broken while they run
katex.min.css references fonts/KaTeX_*.woff2 by relative path; without vendoring all 20 faces the math silently falls back to a system font with wrong metrics
KaTeX does not lay out correctly in quirks mode, so the document starts with <!DOCTYPE html> and a real <head>/<body>

long single-line KaTeX display formulas overflow narrow panel columns and get visually clipped even inside an overflow-x:auto box; fixed by breaking each statement into a \begin{aligned} block of short lines AND scoping .panel .texblock .katex to 0.9em (0.82em under 1080px)

a branch-and-bound seeded with a heuristic value will silently ECHO that seed if the seed is wrong (an early buggy local search returned impossible values like 0 cross edges for r=3 and the exact search dutifully reported them); fixed by pruning against seed+1 instead of seed and returning a found flag, so the reported minimum is always a partition the DFS actually built

the local search must update its current part index after a move — keeping the pre-move index stale lets the size>1 guard pass twice and empties parts, silently returning partitions with fewer than r parts

cytoscape's node.move({parent}) removes and re-adds the element, so the old reference is dead; every re-parent re-fetches by cy.getElementById, and moves are done OUTSIDE cy.batch() (only the class/style repaint is batched)
a cytoscape compound parent with no children still renders as a stray node, so empty cluster boxes are removed explicitly after every re-parent
cy.fit() must be called after re-parenting because the compound boxes change the bounding box; user zoom/pan are disabled and autoungrabify is on so the hand-authored positions stay meaningful

colouring 15 clusters by identity would need far more categorical hues than any palette safely provides; sidestepped entirely by giving cluster identity to a labelled box and spending the whole colour budget on the one semantic distinction that matters (cross vs internal, paid vs short)

green/red is the classic CVD-confusable pair and the dataviz validator flags it, so every status colour on the page is shipped with a glyph (check / equals / cross) and a written verdict, never as colour alone
ECharts multi-grid charts need explicit xAxisIndex/yAxisIndex on every series plus axisPointer.link to share the crosshair between the bar grid and the slack grid
annotating every failing r cluttered the Petersen chart (three overlapping markPoint labels), so only the FIRST failing r is annotated — which is also the pedagogically interesting one
performance.now() does not advance under headless Chrome's virtual time, so elapsed-time readouts show 0.0 ms in a screenshot harness while being real in a normal browser; the page says so
